description: Blocks from the Simulink Math Operations, Logic and Bit Operations and Lookup Tables libraries, plus the signal-routing switches that are normally wired to logic signals. These are the arithmetic, comparison, bit-manipulation and table-interpolation primitives used to build the algorithmic part of a model, and every one of them is fully configurable from MATLAB with add_block and set_param.

tools.name: Gain
tools.description: Multiplies the input by a constant, vector or matrix value and outputs the result. The Multiplication parameter selects element-wise multiplication or one of three matrix forms (K*u, u*K, or K*u treating u as a vector), so the same block covers scalar scaling and matrix transformation. Use it for any fixed coefficient in a model: controller gains, unit conversions, sign inversion, or state-feedback matrices. The gain value can be a MATLAB expression or workspace variable, which makes it the standard hook for parameter sweeps and tuning.
tools.usage: Simulink > Math Operations > Gain (also Simulink > Commonly Used Blocks > Gain)

parameters.name: Gain
parameters.description: Value to multiply the input by. Accepts a numeric literal, MATLAB expression or workspace variable name, e.g. '2.5' or 'Kp'.

parameters.name: Multiplication
parameters.description: Multiplication mode: 'Element-wise(K.*u)' (default), 'Matrix(K*u)', 'Matrix(u*K)' or 'Matrix(K*u) (u vector)'.

parameters.name: ParamDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Data type of the Gain parameter itself, e.g. 'Inherit: Inherit via internal rule' or 'fixdt(1,16,2^-10,0)'.

parameters.name: ParamMin
parameters.description: Minimum value the gain parameter may take; used for range checking and fixed-point autoscaling.

parameters.name: ParamMax
parameters.description: Maximum value the gain parameter may take.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output signal data type, e.g. 'Inherit: Inherit via internal rule', 'double', 'single', 'fixdt(1,16,0)'.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Sample time; '-1' inherits from the driving block.

parameters.name: SaturateOnIntegerOverflow
parameters.description: 'on' saturates integer/fixed-point results instead of wrapping.

tools.notes: For a gain you want to drag at runtime use Slider Gain instead. For a gain that comes in on a signal line, use a Product block: Gain only accepts a dialog value. In matrix modes the gain dimensions must be compatible with the input or Simulink errors at compile time rather than at simulation start.

tools.name: Sum
tools.description: Adds and subtracts its inputs according to a list of signs, or sums the elements of a single vector or matrix input. The Inputs parameter is a sign string such as '++', '+-' or '+-+', where the character '|' inserts a blank space on the icon for layout; setting Inputs to a plain integer means that many '+' ports. Use it for every summing junction, error computation and accumulator in a diagram. The Add, Subtract and Sum of Elements blocks in the library are the same block preset with different Inputs and IconShape values.
tools.usage: Simulink > Math Operations > Sum (also Simulink > Commonly Used Blocks > Sum)

parameters.name: Inputs
parameters.description: Sign list such as '++', '+-', '|+-+' or a positive integer giving the number of '+' inputs. A single '+' with a vector input sums the elements.

parameters.name: IconShape
parameters.description: 'round' (default circular junction) or 'rectangular'.

parameters.name: CollapseMode
parameters.description: 'All dimensions' or 'Specified dimension' — controls element summation when there is only one input port.

parameters.name: CollapseDim
parameters.description: Dimension index to sum over when CollapseMode is 'Specified dimension'.

parameters.name: InputSameDT
parameters.description: 'on' requires all input ports to carry the same data type.

parameters.name: AccumDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Data type of the internal accumulator, important for fixed-point overflow behaviour.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output signal data type.

parameters.name: SaturateOnIntegerOverflow
parameters.description: 'on' saturates rather than wraps on integer overflow.

tools.notes: A feedback path that goes through a Sum with no delay or integrator creates an algebraic loop; break it with a Unit Delay or Memory block. For fixed-point models set AccumDataTypeStr wide enough that partial sums cannot overflow even when the final result fits. Sum of Elements is the same block with Inputs '+' and a vector input.

tools.name: Product
tools.description: Multiplies (and optionally divides) its inputs element-wise, or performs true matrix multiplication and inversion when Multiplication is set to 'Matrix(*)'. Like Sum, the Inputs parameter is either an integer port count or a sign string of '*' and '/' characters, so a single block can compute a*b/c. With one input port it collapses the elements of a vector or matrix into a product. Use it wherever a gain is not constant, for normalisation, and for matrix algebra inside a diagram.
tools.usage: Simulink > Math Operations > Product (also Simulink > Commonly Used Blocks > Product)

parameters.name: Inputs
parameters.description: Number of input ports as an integer, or a string of '*' and '/' characters such as '**/' defining per-port multiply/divide.

parameters.name: Multiplication
parameters.description: 'Element-wise(.*)' (default) or 'Matrix(*)'. Matrix mode with a single '/' input computes a matrix inverse.

parameters.name: CollapseMode
parameters.description: 'All dimensions' or 'Specified dimension' when collapsing a single input into a product.

parameters.name: CollapseDim
parameters.description: Dimension index used when CollapseMode is 'Specified dimension'.

parameters.name: InputSameDT
parameters.description: 'on' requires all inputs to have the same data type.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output signal data type.

parameters.name: RndMeth
parameters.description: Rounding mode for fixed-point results: 'Floor', 'Ceiling', 'Nearest', 'Round', 'Convergent', 'Zero' or 'Simplest'.

parameters.name: SaturateOnIntegerOverflow
parameters.description: 'on' saturates rather than wraps on integer overflow.

tools.notes: The Matrix Multiply and Product of Elements blocks in the library are this same block with different Multiplication and Inputs presets. Division by a signal that can reach zero produces Inf or NaN and will usually stall a variable-step solver — clamp the denominator with a Saturation or MinMax block first.

tools.name: Divide
tools.description: A preset of the Product block whose Inputs string is '*/', so the first port is the numerator and the second the divisor. It performs element-wise division by default and matrix right-division (or inversion) when Multiplication is set to 'Matrix(*)'. Use it for ratios, normalisation by a measured quantity, and any quotient whose divisor arrives on a signal line rather than as a dialog constant.
tools.usage: Simulink > Math Operations > Divide

parameters.name: Inputs
parameters.description: Sign string of '*' and '/' characters; default '*/' gives one multiply port and one divide port.

parameters.name: Multiplication
parameters.description: 'Element-wise(.*)' (default) or 'Matrix(*)' for matrix division/inversion.

parameters.name: InputSameDT
parameters.description: 'on' requires all inputs to have the same data type.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output signal data type.

parameters.name: RndMeth
parameters.description: Rounding mode applied to fixed-point and integer quotients.

parameters.name: SaturateOnIntegerOverflow
parameters.description: 'on' saturates rather than wraps on integer overflow.

tools.notes: Integer division truncates toward the mode set by RndMeth, and integer division by zero is a run-time error rather than Inf. Reciprocal of a single input is cheaper with Math Function set to 'reciprocal'.

tools.name: Abs
tools.description: Outputs the absolute value of the input, applied element-wise to vectors and matrices, and the complex magnitude for complex inputs. Zero-crossing detection is enabled by default so a variable-step solver places a time step exactly where the input changes sign, keeping the corner in the output sharp. Use it for error magnitudes, rectification, and anywhere a sign-independent quantity is needed.
tools.usage: Simulink > Math Operations > Abs

parameters.name: ZeroCross
parameters.description: 'on' (default) enables zero-crossing detection at the sign change; turn it off if the extra solver events slow the simulation.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output signal data type.

parameters.name: SaturateOnIntegerOverflow
parameters.description: 'on' saturates on overflow. Relevant because abs(intmin) is not representable in a signed integer type.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Sample time; '-1' inherits.

parameters.name: OutMin
parameters.description: Lower bound used for range checking and fixed-point autoscaling.

parameters.name: OutMax
parameters.description: Upper bound used for range checking and fixed-point autoscaling.

tools.notes: For a signed integer input, abs of the most negative value overflows; with SaturateOnIntegerOverflow off the result wraps back to that same negative number. For complex signals use Complex to Magnitude-Angle if you also need the phase.

tools.name: Sign
tools.description: Returns 1 when the input is positive, 0 when it is exactly zero and -1 when it is negative, element-wise. It is the signum function and is the standard way to extract direction from a velocity, error or force signal. Use it to build Coulomb friction models, bang-bang control laws and direction flags. Zero-crossing detection is on by default so the solver lands on the discontinuity.
tools.usage: Simulink > Math Operations > Sign

parameters.name: ZeroCross
parameters.description: 'on' (default) enables zero-crossing detection so a variable-step solver resolves the sign change exactly.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Sample time; '-1' inherits from the driving block.

tools.notes: Sign output is exactly 0 at zero input, which differs from a Relational Operator comparison and matters in friction models — combine with Dead Zone or the Coulomb & Viscous Friction block if you need a non-zero breakaway force. Chattering around zero in a feedback loop is a classic cause of very small solver step sizes.

tools.name: Sqrt
tools.description: Computes a square-root family function selected by the Operator parameter: 'sqrt' for u^0.5, 'signedSqrt' for sign(u)*sqrt(|u|), and 'rSqrt' for the reciprocal square root u^-0.5. For fixed-point and embedded targets the AlgorithmType parameter chooses between an exact computation and an iterative Newton-Raphson approximation with a configurable iteration count. Use it for magnitudes, RMS calculations and norm computations.
tools.usage: Simulink > Math Operations > Sqrt (the Signed Sqrt and Reciprocal Sqrt library blocks are the same block with a different Operator)

parameters.name: Operator
parameters.description: 'sqrt' (default), 'signedSqrt' or 'rSqrt'.

parameters.name: AlgorithmType
parameters.description: 'Exact' (default) or 'Newton-Raphson' for an iterative fixed-point-friendly approximation.

parameters.name: Iterations
parameters.description: Number of Newton-Raphson iterations when AlgorithmType is 'Newton-Raphson'.

parameters.name: OutputSignalType
parameters.description: 'auto', 'real' or 'complex'. Set to 'complex' to allow sqrt of a negative real input.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output signal data type.

parameters.name: IntermediateResultsDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Data type of intermediate results in the iterative algorithm.

tools.notes: With Operator 'sqrt' and a real output type, a negative input produces NaN. Use 'signedSqrt' or set OutputSignalType to 'complex' instead. Newton-Raphson mode is far cheaper in generated fixed-point code but its accuracy depends entirely on Iterations.

tools.name: Math Function
tools.description: Applies one of a menu of common mathematical functions chosen by the Operator parameter, covering exponentials and logarithms ('exp', 'log', 'log10', '2^u', '10^u'), powers ('square', 'pow', 'magnitude^2', 'reciprocal'), complex operations ('conj', 'hermitian'), remainders ('rem', 'mod'), the Euclidean 'hypot' and matrix 'transpose'. One block therefore replaces a dozen special-purpose blocks. Use it for unit conversions on a log scale, power computations, modular arithmetic on counters and quick matrix transposes.
tools.usage: Simulink > Math Operations > Math Function

parameters.name: Operator
parameters.description: Function to apply: 'exp', 'log', '2^u', '10^u', 'log10', 'magnitude^2', 'square', 'pow', 'conj', 'reciprocal', 'hypot', 'rem', 'mod', 'transpose' or 'hermitian'.

parameters.name: AlgorithmType
parameters.description: 'Exact' or 'Newton-Raphson' for the 'reciprocal' operator.

parameters.name: Iterations
parameters.description: Newton-Raphson iteration count when AlgorithmType is 'Newton-Raphson'.

parameters.name: OutputSignalType
parameters.description: 'auto', 'real' or 'complex'.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output signal data type; default 'Inherit: Same as first input'.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Sample time; '-1' inherits.

tools.notes: Operators 'pow', 'hypot', 'rem' and 'mod' take two input ports; the rest take one. 'rem' follows the sign of the dividend while 'mod' follows the sign of the divisor — a frequent source of off-by-a-period bugs in angle wrapping. For floor/ceil/round/fix use the Rounding Function block, and for negation use Unary Minus.

tools.name: Trigonometric Function
tools.description: Computes a trigonometric or hyperbolic function selected by Operator, including the inverse functions, the two-argument 'atan2', and the combined 'sincos' and 'cos + jsin' outputs. For embedded and fixed-point targets the ApproximationMethod parameter switches the implementation from the exact library call to a CORDIC iteration or a lookup table with a configurable number of data points. Use it for kinematics, coordinate rotations, phase computations and oscillator models.
tools.usage: Simulink > Math Operations > Trigonometric Function

parameters.name: Operator
parameters.description: 'sin', 'cos', 'tan', 'asin', 'acos', 'atan', 'atan2', 'sinh', 'cosh', 'tanh', 'asinh', 'acosh', 'atanh', 'sincos' or 'cos + jsin'.

parameters.name: ApproximationMethod
parameters.description: 'None' (exact), 'CORDIC' or 'Lookup' — controls the implementation used in simulation and generated code.

parameters.name: NumberOfIterations
parameters.description: CORDIC iteration count; more iterations means more accuracy and more cycles.

parameters.name: NumberOfDataPoints
parameters.description: Table size when ApproximationMethod is 'Lookup'.

parameters.name: InterpMethod
parameters.description: 'Linear point-slope' or 'Flat' interpolation for the lookup implementation.

parameters.name: AngleUnit
parameters.description: 'radian' (default) or 'revolution' for the input/output angle unit.

parameters.name: OutputSignalType
parameters.description: 'auto', 'real' or 'complex'.

tools.notes: 'atan2' takes two ports (y then x) and is the correct choice for four-quadrant angle recovery — plain 'atan' loses the quadrant. CORDIC and Lookup modes are the only ones supported for fixed-point input types. 'sincos' emits two output ports in one pass, which is cheaper than two separate blocks.

tools.name: MinMax
tools.description: Outputs the minimum or maximum of its inputs, selected by the Function parameter. With several input ports it compares element-wise across the ports; with a single input port it collapses the elements of a vector or matrix down to one extremum. Use it to clamp a signal against a variable limit, to select the more severe of two demands, or to pick a peak out of a bus of measurements.
tools.usage: Simulink > Math Operations > MinMax

parameters.name: Function
parameters.description: 'min' (default) or 'max'.

parameters.name: Inputs
parameters.description: Number of input ports. With one port the block reduces the elements of that signal.

parameters.name: CollapseMode
parameters.description: 'All dimensions' or 'Specified dimension' when reducing a single input.

parameters.name: CollapseDim
parameters.description: Dimension index used when CollapseMode is 'Specified dimension'.

parameters.name: ZeroCross
parameters.description: 'on' (default) enables zero-crossing detection where the winning input changes.

parameters.name: InputSameDT
parameters.description: 'on' requires all input ports to share a data type.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output signal data type.

tools.notes: A min/max pair is the standard way to saturate against limits that arrive on signal lines; the Saturation block only accepts dialog limits (use Saturation Dynamic for signal-driven limits). NaN propagation is implementation-defined, so filter NaNs upstream. MinMax Running Resettable gives the running extremum over time instead.

tools.name: Logical Operator
tools.description: Performs a boolean operation selected by Operator across its input ports: AND, OR, NAND, NOR, XOR, NXOR or the single-input NOT. Any non-zero input is treated as true, and the output is boolean by default. The IconShape parameter switches between a plain rectangle and the distinctive IEEE gate symbol, which makes logic diagrams readable at a glance. Use it to combine enable flags, fault conditions, comparator outputs and mode selections.
tools.usage: Simulink > Logic and Bit Operations > Logical Operator (also Simulink > Commonly Used Blocks > Logical Operator)

parameters.name: Operator
parameters.description: 'AND' (default), 'OR', 'NAND', 'NOR', 'XOR', 'NXOR' or 'NOT'.

parameters.name: Inputs
parameters.description: Number of input ports; ignored when Operator is 'NOT'.

parameters.name: IconShape
parameters.description: 'rectangular' (default) or 'distinctive' to draw the standard gate symbol.

parameters.name: AllPortsSameDT
parameters.description: 'on' requires every input port to have the same data type.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output data type: 'boolean' (default), an inheritance rule, or a fixed-point type such as 'fixdt(1,16)'.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Sample time; '-1' inherits.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Logic and Bit Operations/Logical Operator', 'mathDemo/And');
set_param('mathDemo/And', 'Operator', 'AND', 'Inputs', '3', 'IconShape', 'distinctive');
tools.notes: This block works on whole values, not on the bits inside them — use Bitwise Operator for bit masks. With a vector input and one port, XOR reduces the elements. Feeding a double signal works but is wasteful in generated code; convert to boolean upstream with a Relational Operator or Compare To Zero.

tools.name: Relational Operator
tools.description: Compares two inputs with the relation selected by Operator and outputs a boolean true or false, element-wise. Besides the six comparisons it also offers the single-input tests 'isInf', 'isNaN' and 'isFinite', which are the standard way to detect numerical blow-up inside a running model. Use it to build thresholds, limit detectors, state transition conditions and Switch control signals.
tools.usage: Simulink > Logic and Bit Operations > Relational Operator (also Simulink > Commonly Used Blocks > Relational Operator)

parameters.name: Operator
parameters.description: '==', '~=', '<', '<=' (default), '>=', '>', or the one-input tests 'isInf', 'isNaN', 'isFinite'.

parameters.name: InputSameDT
parameters.description: 'on' requires both inputs to have the same data type.

parameters.name: LogicOutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output data type, normally 'boolean' or an inheritance rule.

parameters.name: ZeroCross
parameters.description: 'on' (default) enables zero-crossing detection so the solver lands exactly on the threshold crossing.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Sample time; '-1' inherits.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Logic and Bit Operations/Relational Operator', 'mathDemo/Cmp');
set_param('mathDemo/Cmp', 'Operator', '>=', 'LogicOutDataTypeStr', 'boolean');
tools.notes: Comparing floating-point signals with '==' is almost never what you want; compare a difference against a tolerance instead. When one operand is a constant, Compare To Constant is a single-port equivalent that generates tighter code. Selecting 'isInf', 'isNaN' or 'isFinite' removes the second input port.

tools.name: Compare To Zero
tools.description: Compares a single input against zero using the relation set by relop and outputs boolean true or false. It is a masked convenience wrapper around Relational Operator with a hard-wired zero constant, so it needs only one wire and produces compact generated code. Use it for sign tests, zero-speed detection, residual checks and enabling logic driven by an error signal.
tools.usage: Simulink > Logic and Bit Operations > Compare To Zero

parameters.name: relop
parameters.description: Relational operator applied against zero: '==', '~=', '<', '<=', '>=' or '>'.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output data type: 'boolean' (default) or 'uint8'.

parameters.name: ZeroCross
parameters.description: 'on' (default) enables zero-crossing detection at the comparison boundary.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Logic and Bit Operations/Compare To Zero', 'mathDemo/IsPos');
set_param('mathDemo/IsPos', 'relop', '>', 'OutDataTypeStr', 'boolean');
tools.notes: Compare To Constant is the same idea with an arbitrary constant, set through its 'const' parameter. Because these are masked subsystems, set_param must use the mask parameter names ('relop', 'const'), not the underlying Relational Operator names.

tools.name: Bitwise Operator
tools.description: Performs a bit-level AND, OR, NAND, NOR, XOR or NOT on integer or fixed-point operands, either between several input ports or between one input and a constant bit mask. When UseBitMask is on the block takes a single input and applies the value in BitMask, which is the usual way to test, set or clear status flags in a register image. Use it for protocol decoding, fault-word packing and any hardware register manipulation inside a model.
tools.usage: Simulink > Logic and Bit Operations > Bitwise Operator

parameters.name: logicop
parameters.description: Bit operation to perform: 'AND' (default), 'OR', 'NAND', 'NOR', 'XOR' or 'NOT'.

parameters.name: UseBitMask
parameters.description: 'on' (default) uses the dialog BitMask against a single input; 'off' enables multiple input ports.

parameters.name: NumInputPorts
parameters.description: Number of input ports when UseBitMask is 'off'.

parameters.name: BitMask
parameters.description: Mask value applied when UseBitMask is 'on'. Accepts decimal, hexadecimal or expressions such as bin2dec('11011001').

parameters.name: BitMaskRealWorld
parameters.description: 'Real World Value' or 'Stored Integer' — how the mask is interpreted for a fixed-point input.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Logic and Bit Operations/Bitwise Operator', 'mathDemo/Mask');
set_param('mathDemo/Mask', 'logicop', 'AND', 'UseBitMask', 'on', 'BitMask', 'bin2dec(''00001111'')');
tools.notes: The input must be an integer or fixed-point type; feeding a double is an error. This block does not shift — use Shift Arithmetic for that. Do not confuse it with Logical Operator, which treats each whole value as a single true/false.

tools.name: Shift Arithmetic
tools.description: Shifts the bits of an integer or fixed-point input left or right, and independently shifts the position of the binary point, so it covers both bit manipulation and cheap power-of-two scaling. The number of places can come from the dialog or from a second input port, and the direction can be fixed or bidirectional (negative values reverse the direction). Use it for fast multiply/divide by powers of two, fixed-point rescaling without a multiply, and packing or unpacking bit fields.
tools.usage: Simulink > Logic and Bit Operations > Shift Arithmetic

parameters.name: BitShiftNumberSource
parameters.description: 'Dialog' (default) or 'Input port' — where the shift amount comes from.

parameters.name: BitShiftDirection
parameters.description: 'Left', 'Right' or 'Bidirectional'.

parameters.name: BitShiftNumber
parameters.description: Number of bit positions to shift when BitShiftNumberSource is 'Dialog'.

parameters.name: BinPtShiftNumber
parameters.description: Number of places to shift the binary point; changes the scaling without touching the stored bits.

parameters.name: DiagnosticForOORShift
parameters.description: Action on an out-of-range shift value: 'Error', 'Warning' or 'None'.

parameters.name: CheckOORBitShift
parameters.description: 'on' keeps the out-of-range shift check in generated code.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Logic and Bit Operations/Shift Arithmetic', 'mathDemo/Shift');
set_param('mathDemo/Shift', 'BitShiftDirection', 'Right', 'BitShiftNumber', '3', 'BinPtShiftNumber', '0');
tools.notes: A right shift on a signed type is arithmetic, so the sign bit is replicated and the result rounds toward negative infinity, not toward zero. Shifting the binary point alone costs nothing at run time — it only reinterprets the scaling — which makes it the cheapest possible fixed-point rescale.

tools.name: 1-D Lookup Table
tools.description: Approximates a one-dimensional function y = f(x) by interpolating a table of breakpoints and output values. The InterpMethod parameter selects flat (hold), linear point-slope, linear Lagrange, nearest, cubic spline or Akima spline interpolation, and ExtrapMethod controls behaviour beyond the last breakpoint. Use it for sensor calibration curves, empirical engine or motor maps, efficiency curves, and anywhere a measured characteristic replaces an analytic formula.
tools.usage: Simulink > Lookup Tables > 1-D Lookup Table

parameters.name: Table
parameters.description: Vector of table output values, one per breakpoint.

parameters.name: BreakpointsForDimension1
parameters.description: Vector of monotonically increasing input breakpoints.

parameters.name: BreakpointsSpecification
parameters.description: 'Explicit values' (default) or 'Even spacing', which replaces the vector with a first point, spacing and number of points.

parameters.name: BreakpointsForDimension1FirstPoint
parameters.description: First breakpoint value when BreakpointsSpecification is 'Even spacing'.

parameters.name: BreakpointsForDimension1Spacing
parameters.description: Breakpoint spacing when BreakpointsSpecification is 'Even spacing'.

parameters.name: InterpMethod
parameters.description: 'Linear point-slope' (default), 'Flat', 'Nearest', 'Linear Lagrange', 'Cubic spline' or 'Akima spline'.

parameters.name: ExtrapMethod
parameters.description: 'Linear' (default), 'Clip' or 'Cubic spline' behaviour outside the breakpoint range.

parameters.name: DataSpecification
parameters.description: 'Table and breakpoints' (default) or 'Lookup table object' to reference a Simulink.LookupTable object.

parameters.name: IndexSearchMethod
parameters.description: 'Binary search' (default), 'Evenly spaced points' or 'Linear search'.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output signal data type.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Lookup Tables/1-D Lookup Table', 'mathDemo/Curve');
set_param('mathDemo/Curve', 'BreakpointsForDimension1', '[0 1 2 3 4]', 'Table', '[0 0.5 0.9 1.0 1.0]', 'InterpMethod', 'Linear point-slope', 'ExtrapMethod', 'Clip');
tools.notes: Breakpoints must be strictly monotonically increasing or the block errors at compile time. 'Linear' extrapolation can produce wild values far outside the table — 'Clip' is usually the safe choice for physical characteristics. Set IndexSearchMethod to 'Evenly spaced points' when the breakpoints really are evenly spaced: the search becomes a single divide instead of a binary search.

tools.name: 2-D Lookup Table
tools.description: Approximates a two-dimensional function z = f(x, y) by interpolating a rectangular grid of table data against two independent breakpoint vectors. It takes two input ports and supports the same interpolation and extrapolation methods as the 1-D block. Use it for maps that depend on two operating conditions — engine torque versus speed and throttle, compressor efficiency versus pressure ratio and flow, or a gain schedule over two scheduling variables.
tools.usage: Simulink > Lookup Tables > 2-D Lookup Table

parameters.name: Table
parameters.description: Matrix of table data. Its size must be numel(BreakpointsForDimension1) by numel(BreakpointsForDimension2).

parameters.name: BreakpointsForDimension1
parameters.description: Monotonically increasing breakpoint vector for the first (row) input.

parameters.name: BreakpointsForDimension2
parameters.description: Monotonically increasing breakpoint vector for the second (column) input.

parameters.name: BreakpointsSpecification
parameters.description: 'Explicit values' or 'Even spacing'.

parameters.name: InterpMethod
parameters.description: 'Linear point-slope' (default), 'Flat', 'Nearest', 'Linear Lagrange', 'Cubic spline' or 'Akima spline'.

parameters.name: ExtrapMethod
parameters.description: 'Linear', 'Clip' or 'Cubic spline'.

parameters.name: DataSpecification
parameters.description: 'Table and breakpoints' or 'Lookup table object'.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output signal data type.

tools.notes: A transposed table is the most common mistake: dimension 1 indexes the first input port and corresponds to the rows of Table. For more than two inputs use n-D Lookup Table, and if several tables share the same breakpoints split the search out into a Prelookup block so the index is computed only once.

tools.name: n-D Lookup Table
tools.description: Generalises table interpolation to between 1 and 30 dimensions, with one input port per dimension and one breakpoint vector each. NumberOfTableDimensions sets the dimensionality and the block then exposes BreakpointsForDimension1 through BreakpointsForDimension30. Use it for multi-variable calibration maps, high-dimensional gain schedules, and any characteristic measured over three or more operating variables.
tools.usage: Simulink > Lookup Tables > n-D Lookup Table

parameters.name: NumberOfTableDimensions
parameters.description: Number of table dimensions, 1 to 30. Determines how many input ports appear.

parameters.name: Table
parameters.description: N-dimensional array of table data whose size matches the breakpoint vectors in order.

parameters.name: BreakpointsForDimension1
parameters.description: Breakpoint vector for dimension 1; BreakpointsForDimension2 ... BreakpointsForDimension30 follow the same pattern.

parameters.name: BreakpointsSpecification
parameters.description: 'Explicit values' or 'Even spacing'.

parameters.name: InterpMethod
parameters.description: 'Linear point-slope' (default), 'Flat', 'Nearest', 'Linear Lagrange', 'Cubic spline' or 'Akima spline'.

parameters.name: ExtrapMethod
parameters.description: 'Linear', 'Clip' or 'Cubic spline'.

parameters.name: IndexSearchMethod
parameters.description: 'Binary search', 'Evenly spaced points' or 'Linear search'.

parameters.name: BeginIndexSearchUsingPreviousIndexResult
parameters.description: 'on' starts each search from the previous result, which is much faster for slowly varying inputs.

parameters.name: DataSpecification
parameters.description: 'Table and breakpoints' or 'Lookup table object'.

tools.notes: Memory grows as the product of the breakpoint counts, so a five-dimensional table with 20 points per axis is 3.2 million entries — check the generated-code footprint before committing. Cubic and Akima spline methods are not supported for fixed-point data types.

tools.name: Prelookup
tools.description: Performs only the breakpoint search half of a table lookup: given an input and a breakpoint vector it outputs the index of the enclosing interval and the fractional distance within it. Pair it with one or more Interpolation Using Prelookup blocks that share the same breakpoints so the expensive search runs once instead of once per table. Use it whenever several maps are indexed by the same scheduling variable, which is the normal situation in engine and gain-scheduling models.
tools.usage: Simulink > Lookup Tables > Prelookup

parameters.name: BreakpointsData
parameters.description: Monotonically increasing breakpoint vector.

parameters.name: BreakpointsSpecification
parameters.description: 'Explicit values' (default) or 'Even spacing'.

parameters.name: BreakpointsFirstPoint
parameters.description: First breakpoint when using even spacing.

parameters.name: BreakpointsSpacing
parameters.description: Spacing between breakpoints when using even spacing.

parameters.name: BreakpointsNumPoints
parameters.description: Number of breakpoints when using even spacing.

parameters.name: OutputSelection
parameters.description: 'Index and fraction' (default, two ports) or 'Index and fraction as bus' (single bus port).

parameters.name: IndexSearchMethod
parameters.description: 'Binary search' (default), 'Evenly spaced points' or 'Linear search'.

parameters.name: BeginIndexSearchUsingPreviousIndexResult
parameters.description: 'on' seeds each search with the previous index for faster lookup of slowly varying signals.

parameters.name: ExtrapMethod
parameters.description: 'Clip' or 'Linear' behaviour outside the breakpoint range.

parameters.name: DiagnosticForOutOfRangeInput
parameters.description: 'None', 'Warning' or 'Error' when the input falls outside the breakpoints.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Lookup Tables/Prelookup', 'mathDemo/PreRPM');
set_param('mathDemo/PreRPM', 'BreakpointsData', '[800 1600 2400 3200 4000]', 'OutputSelection', 'Index and fraction', 'IndexSearchMethod', 'Binary search');
tools.notes: The index/fraction pair must be fed to an Interpolation Using Prelookup block configured with matching table dimensions, otherwise the results are silently wrong. Setting OutputSelection to the bus form keeps the diagram tidy when routing to several interpolation blocks.

tools.name: Interpolation Using Prelookup
tools.description: Consumes the index and fraction produced by one Prelookup block per dimension and interpolates the table data to produce the output. Splitting search from interpolation this way lets many tables share a single search, and it also lets the sub-table selection feature pick a slice of a larger table at run time. Use it as the second half of every multi-table gain schedule or calibration map.
tools.usage: Simulink > Lookup Tables > Interpolation Using Prelookup

parameters.name: NumberOfTableDimensions
parameters.description: Number of dimensions to interpolate; sets how many index/fraction input pairs appear.

parameters.name: Table
parameters.description: Table data array, sized to match the Prelookup breakpoint vectors.

parameters.name: TableSpecification
parameters.description: 'Explicit values' or 'Lookup table object'.

parameters.name: InterpMethod
parameters.description: 'Linear point-slope' (default), 'Flat', 'Nearest', 'Linear Lagrange', 'Cubic spline' or 'Akima spline'.

parameters.name: ExtrapMethod
parameters.description: 'Linear' or 'Clip' behaviour for out-of-range index/fraction pairs.

parameters.name: RequireIndexFractionAsBus
parameters.description: 'on' accepts the index and fraction as a single bus, matching Prelookup's bus output mode.

parameters.name: ValidIndexMayReachLast
parameters.description: 'on' allows the index to equal the last breakpoint index.

parameters.name: NumSelectionDims
parameters.description: Number of sub-table selection dimensions used to slice a larger table at run time.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output signal data type.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Lookup Tables/Interpolation Using Prelookup', 'mathDemo/InterpTorque');
set_param('mathDemo/InterpTorque', 'NumberOfTableDimensions', '2', 'Table', 'torqueMap', 'InterpMethod', 'Linear point-slope');
tools.notes: The table dimensions here must agree with the number and order of the Prelookup blocks feeding it. Turning on RemoveProtectionIndex removes the range check from generated code, which is faster but will read out of bounds if a Prelookup upstream is ever misconfigured.

tools.name: Direct Lookup Table (n-D)
tools.description: Indexes directly into an n-dimensional table with zero-based integer inputs and returns the selected element, column or 2-D plane — no interpolation and no breakpoint search. Because the inputs are indices rather than physical values, it is the fastest lookup available and generates a single array access. Use it for state machines with tabulated outputs, decision matrices, character or symbol tables, and any case where the input is already an enumerated index.
tools.usage: Simulink > Lookup Tables > Direct Lookup Table (n-D)

parameters.name: NumberOfTableDimensions
parameters.description: Number of table dimensions, 1 to 30.

parameters.name: Table
parameters.description: Table data array. Ignored when TableIsInput is 'on'.

parameters.name: TableIsInput
parameters.description: 'on' makes the table arrive on an input port instead of the dialog, so it can change at run time.

parameters.name: InputsSelectThisObjectFromTable
parameters.description: What each lookup returns: 'Element' (default), 'Column' or '2-D Matrix'.

parameters.name: DiagnosticForOutOfRangeInput
parameters.description: 'None', 'Warning' or 'Error' when an index falls outside the table.

parameters.name: RemoveProtectionInput
parameters.description: 'on' removes the range check from generated code for speed.

parameters.name: TableDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Data type of the table data.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Sample time; '-1' inherits.

tools.notes: Indices are zero-based, unlike MATLAB's one-based indexing — this is the single most common error with this block. Non-integer inputs are truncated. If you need interpolation between entries use 1-D/n-D Lookup Table instead.

tools.name: Switch
tools.description: Passes the first input through when the second (control) input satisfies the condition set by Criteria, and otherwise passes the third input. The criterion is u2 > Threshold, u2 >= Threshold, or u2 ~= 0, so the block works equally well with a boolean flag or an analog control signal. Use it for mode selection, fault fallback, manual/auto changeover and any if/else in the signal path. Although it lives in Signal Routing it is effectively the primary conditional operator of a Simulink diagram.
tools.usage: Simulink > Signal Routing > Switch (also Simulink > Commonly Used Blocks > Switch)

parameters.name: Criteria
parameters.description: 'u2 > Threshold' (default), 'u2 >= Threshold' or 'u2 ~= 0'.

parameters.name: Threshold
parameters.description: Threshold value compared against the control input; disabled when Criteria is 'u2 ~= 0'.

parameters.name: ZeroCross
parameters.description: 'on' (default) enables zero-crossing detection at the switching point.

parameters.name: InputSameDT
parameters.description: 'on' requires both data inputs to have the same data type.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output signal data type.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Sample time; '-1' inherits.

parameters.name: AllowDiffInputSizes
parameters.description: 'on' allows the two data inputs to have different sizes (variable-size signals).

tools.notes: Both data branches execute every step — Switch selects a value, it does not skip computation. Use an Enabled or If Action Subsystem when you actually need to suppress execution. Switching between two continuous signals introduces a discontinuity; leave ZeroCross on so the variable-step solver resolves it.

tools.name: Multiport Switch
tools.description: Selects one of many data inputs based on the value of the first (control) input, giving an n-way switch or a C-style switch/case in the signal path. DataPortOrder chooses between zero-based indexing, one-based indexing and explicitly specified index values, and an optional default port handles out-of-range control values. Use it for mode tables, gear or state selection, and routing one of several controller outputs to a plant.
tools.usage: Simulink > Signal Routing > Multiport Switch

parameters.name: Inputs
parameters.description: Number of data input ports (in addition to the control port).

parameters.name: DataPortOrder
parameters.description: 'Zero-based contiguous', 'One-based contiguous' (default) or 'Specify indices'.

parameters.name: DataPortIndices
parameters.description: Cell array of index values, e.g. '{1,2,3}', used when DataPortOrder is 'Specify indices'.

parameters.name: DataPortForDefault
parameters.description: 'Last data port' (default) or 'Additional data port' to handle out-of-range control values.

parameters.name: DiagnosticForDefault
parameters.description: 'None', 'Warning' or 'Error' when the control input selects the default case.

parameters.name: InputSameDT
parameters.description: 'on' requires all data inputs to have the same data type.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output signal data type.

parameters.name: ZeroCross
parameters.description: 'on' enables zero-crossing detection at switching points.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Signal Routing/Multiport Switch', 'mathDemo/Mode');
set_param('mathDemo/Mode', 'Inputs', '3', 'DataPortOrder', 'One-based contiguous', 'DataPortForDefault', 'Additional data port');
tools.notes: Getting DataPortOrder wrong is the usual failure: a zero-based control signal into a one-based block silently selects the neighbouring port. The control input is truncated toward zero if it is not an integer. An enumerated control type pairs well with 'Specify indices'.

tools.name: Manual Switch
tools.description: A two-input toggle with no control port: you double-click it in the canvas to flip which input reaches the output, and the setting is stored in the sw parameter so it can also be changed from a script during or between simulations. There is no cost in generated code because the choice is fixed at build time. Use it for quick what-if comparisons, switching a plant between a linear and a nonlinear model, or selecting between a test signal and a live input while debugging.
tools.usage: Simulink > Signal Routing > Manual Switch

parameters.name: sw
parameters.description: Which input is passed through: '1' selects the first (top) input, '0' selects the second (bottom) input.

parameters.name: varsize
parameters.description: 'on' allows the two inputs to have different sizes.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Sample time; '-1' inherits.

tools.notes: Because it is a masked block, set_param must use the mask parameter name 'sw'. Changing sw during a running simulation takes effect immediately, which makes it handy for interactive testing but unsuitable for logic that must be reproducible — use Switch with a real control signal for that. Manual Variant Sink/Source serve the same purpose at the variant level.
